title: AI Ready Coding Agents Playbook
scope: Practical, provider-neutral operating rules with current adapters for Codex, Claude Code, and Kimi Code.
portable_rules: Keep always-on repository instructions short and operational.
Give every non-trivial task an executable definition of done.
Use read-only exploration before writing when the change surface is unclear.
Keep final write ownership clear even when research runs in parallel.
Use deterministic tests, builds, linters, and type checks as judges.
Move repeated procedures into Skills instead of retyping prompts.
Move repeated corrections into durable repository instructions or scoped rules.
Use hooks or permissions for rules that must be enforced, not prompt text alone.
Start a fresh context when the objective changes materially.
Do not claim success when required verification could not run.

task_modes.goal: Map evidence, files, dependencies, and the smallest likely change surface.
Make the smallest defensible change and run named verification.
Review the diff for correctness, regression, security, data loss, and missing tests.

hints: Layer AGENTS.md from repository root toward the working directory.
Use parallel agents first for read-heavy independent work.
Keep one clear owner for write-heavy changes.
Test command rules with execpolicy instead of assuming they match.
Keep CLAUDE.md focused on information needed in nearly every session.
Use path-scoped rules for directory or language-specific instructions.
Use hooks for deterministic must-run actions.
Use a fresh context for final review after a large implementation.
Use .agents/skills for workflows shared with Codex.
Do not use hooks as the only security boundary because hook failures are fail-open.
Use broad auto-approval only in trusted or strongly sandboxed environments.
